doc.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21

title: Following Joe Oliver at the Dreamland and first band
summary: Mugsy bought records, followed Oliver at the Dreamland and Royal Garden, learned his mute style, and played in a Clark Street group.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I got some records. I bought some Jeanette records with Joe Alvarez. Oh yeah. So I was going on the south side, and I wanted to find out where Joe was working. At that time, he was working at the Dreamland. Yeah. 35th Estate. Yeah. One of them. He used to have Wednesday matinees. Oh yeah? So. I guess they didn't have any relish. They'd go down there every Wednesday afternoon. Mm-hmm. Sit on the bed. They'd let us sit. They'd sit up in the balcony and drink Coca-Cola. Oh, just move around. And then, I think after that, Joe went to California for a while. That's right. And he came back. He went to work at the Royal Garden. And I was down there all the time. I was down there pretty early night. Was he especially your favorite? And were you following him? Yes. Personally, like more than anybody else. Yeah. I followed him more than... That was your man. Yeah. I had a driving style, you know. Yeah. Well, I liked that. Yeah. But were you playing yourself by the style? Oh, yes. I was playing professionally then. You were playing professionally? Oh, yes. And I liked the way Joe used mute, you know. That's where I got that from. Just was second nature then. Well, how did you first... I mean, how did you first... Why did you... When you first started, what kind of a band did you yourself play with? The jazz band. The jazz band. The jazz band. Elmer Schovel was in the band, George Brunus. Oh, yeah? Oh, yeah. What band was this? It wasn't the name of a band. We worked at a place called the Blacks Palm Garden, West North Avenue in Chicago. What kind of tunes did you play? Beg your pardon? What kind of tunes did you play? We played all the standard tunes in the day then. We never played any pop tunes. It was all standard tunes, blues and all that. Oh, yeah? Oh, yeah. Homer Schovel, he was a good piano player. Yeah. He was the only one that could read in a band. Uh-huh. Then I later started studying, learned how to read. Because that helps you out. You have to learn how to read. Sometimes. That's the way it was out, man. Pickle and my brother was on his tune read. I was right. In the afternoon. Joe was going to be much faster than he did. I used to listen to Joe sit out on the curb stomp when he worked at the Dreamland. That's before the, before he worked at the Dreamland, he used to work at a place called the Peking. Yes. And that's a police station now, upstairs. Was that an after hours place? No. Regular club. Oh, yes. Well, that time they used to stay open. Nine o'clock, five, six, seven o'clock in the morning. Oh, yeah? And I'd sit out on the curb stomp and just listen to Joe. Because he wouldn't let me in there.
